back: Protocols that give an encrypted, authenticated connection between client and server; used by HTTPS.
Client asks; server sends certificate; client checks it; client sends session key encrypted with the server's public key; server decrypts with its private key; session uses symmetric encryption.
Links a public key to its owner's identity; issued and signed by a certificate authority.
Owner's name or domain, public key, issuing CA, serial number, validity dates, CA's digital signature.
A trusted organisation that checks identity and issues signed certificates.
A digest of the message encrypted with the sender's private key; checked with the sender's public key by comparing digests.
Expired or not yet valid; domain name does not match; issuer not trusted (including self-signed); revoked.
Symmetric encryption is much faster than asymmetric, so the public key only protects the session key.
